Two dead in flooding in Spain’s Catalonia region

Reuters

04 October, 2026 03:00 pm IST

Facebook

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

Oct 4 (Reuters) – Two people have died and another was missing after heavy rains and flooding in Spain’s Catalonia region, authorities said on Sunday.

Catalan leader Salvador Illa confirmed the death of a man after a wall collapsed in Tordera, a town to the north of Barcelona, in a message on his social media account on Sunday.

Another person died in Montornès del Vallès, firefighters said on Sunday, while emergency services were searching for a missing person in Pineda de Mar, a town 52 km (32 miles) to the north of Barcelona.

Show Full Article

Catalan authorities issued a red alert warning and urged people to stay inside from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Saturday until Sunday at 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) because a “mini-hurricane” could hit the northeastern region, with more heavy rain forecast.

Homes were flooded and cars left submerged in Bellvitge and Cornella near Barcelona after torrential rain on Saturday. Ducks swam in huge puddles that formed on motorways in Barcelona.

Sarai Sarroca, director of regional weather service Meteocat, said on Saturday that the core of an exceptional weather system was over the Mediterranean and a “mini-hurricane” could move over land in Catalonia.

Flights were cancelled or delayed at Barcelona airport, La Vanguardia newspaper reported on Saturday.

All local trains were disrupted by the deluge. Shops shut early, football matches were called off and a performance of Verdi’s Aida at Barcelona’s Liceu opera house was cancelled.

(Reporting by Graham KeeleyEditing by David Goodman)

Philippines accuses Chinese coast guard of blocking law enforcement mission near Thitu

Reuters

04 October, 2026 03:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MANILA, Oct 4 (Reuters) – The Philippine Coast Guard said on Sunday Chinese vessels obstructed a Philippine law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near the Manila-held Thitu Island in the South China Sea.

It described the presence of a Chinese navy helicopter as an “unnecessary act of intimidation”. It was the latest in a series of recent maritime confrontations between Manila and Beijing.

• The operation involved personnel from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Philippine Navy and Philippine National Police Maritime Group responding to a report of suspected blast fishing near Sandy Cays 2 and 3, about three nautical miles west of Thitu Island, known in the Philippines as Pag-asa.

Show Full Article

• The PCG said two China Coast Guard vessels sounded their horns, radio-challenged the Philippine team and later shadowed and blocked its boats. A People’s Liberation Army Navy helicopter also circled above the Philippine personnel four times.

• The Philippine team ordered the foreign fishing vessel to stop and radioed it several times, but the vessel ignored the orders and sailed southwest toward Subi Reef, one of seven artificial islands China has built in the Spratlys to support its sovereignty claims.

• Philippine authorities ended the pursuit for safety reasons and returned to Thitu.

• The PCG said the China Coast Guard had “no law enforcement authority” in the territorial sea of Thitu and said its actions “made it easier for a suspected violator to escape”. It also rejected any Chinese claim that its vessels had been expelled from the area.

• At just 37 hectares (0.14 square miles), the coral-fringed Thitu is the largest and most prized of the nine Philippines-held features in the Spratly archipelago, located 450 km (280 miles) from the mainland.

• Separately, the military said a Chinese J-16 fighter jet repeatedly approached and manoeuvred close to a Philippine patrol aircraft over the disputed Scarborough Shoal on Saturday, creating an aviation safety risk.

• The Armed Forces of the Philippines said the incident was part of a “recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behaviour” against Philippine vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations.

• The Chinese Embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the weekend incidents.

(Reporting by Karen Lema ; Additional reporting by Greg Torode; Editing by Sonali Paul)

Government forces seize capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region from rebels

Reuters

04 October, 2026 02:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Oct 4 (Reuters) – Ethiopian government forces and allied militias have regained control of the capital of Tigray, three sources told Reuters on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern region.

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the opposition alliance, said in a statement posted on Facebook it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be “temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else.”

A source close to the pro-government militia, the Tigray Peace Forces, said its fighters entered the centre of Mekelle on Saturday afternoon, followed by the Ethiopian military. A humanitarian source and a Mekelle resident, who asked not to be named, confirmed the city was controlled by government forces.

Show Full Article

The prime minister’s office did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

LOSS OF MEKELLE A MAJOR BLOW FOR TPLF

The taking of Mekelle by pro-government forces is a major loss for the opposition alliance led by the TPLF, which launched a big offensive on September 23 against the Ethiopian military.

Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have made a quick counterattack into Tigray, but analysts say the fighting — the worst escalation since a 2020-2022 civil war — threatens to escalate into a wider regional conflict.

The federal government in Addis Ababa severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea last week, accusing it of supporting the rebel alliance alongside Sudan and Egypt. The three countries deny this.

(Reporting by Ammu Kannampillay; Editing by Silvia Aloisi and Helen Popper)

Haunted by grief, Gaza’s displaced still wait overseas for return

Reuters

04 October, 2026 01:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Nidal al-Mughrabi CAIRO, Oct 4 (Reuters) – Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.

Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war that was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, and who remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their destroyed homes and neighbourhoods.

“I left Gaza and came to Egypt, the land of Kinana (referring to Egypt), but at the same time, this will not be forgotten, my dear brother, it will not be forgotten,” he said.

Show Full Article

“I am waiting for the opportunity, I am waiting for the moment when Gaza becomes stable so I can return to my country, and be a productive member of this country, and be a positive force for the country.”

Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza that was meant to start a process of reconstruction under a technocratic government along with a political process that would lead to an eventual full Israeli withdrawal, little has changed.

Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where Palestinians live, mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies and no prospect of reconstruction soon.

Some 308 members of Hassayna’s extended family were killed when Israeli strikes destroyed a cluster of Gaza City apartment buildings where they had gathered for shelter on November 22, 2023, according to Palestinian authorities.

Among those killed were his wife, four of their adult sons and four small grandchildren including an infant only a few months old.

Hassayna’s oldest son Mohammed is also in Cairo along with his own four children, as is the widow of one of his dead sons with her daughter. He has brothers in the Egyptian capital too.

One daughter was medically evacuated to Turkey with her husband and six children, and another daughter remains in Gaza with her five children although her husband was killed in the attack.

The Israeli military did not respond to a request for comment on the details of the November 22 strike. It said its attacks in Gaza are directed at military targets, while trying to reduce harm to civilians.

ABOUT 7,000 PALESTINIANS HAVE RETURNED TO GAZA

In August, Hassayna watched on video from Cairo as relatives buried 112 family members, including his wife, sons and grandchildren, whose bodies had been recovered from the rubble, with dozens still missing.

Hassayna owned a business selling tools for firefighting and safety equipment in Gaza and some of his goods survived the war. He periodically sells some to fund his stay in Cairo, where he has remarried.

All those who left Gaza were vetted before their departure by both Israel and Egypt, but many have found it hard to return to the territory.

Although some Israeli politicians have urged a policy of encouraging all Gaza’s population to leave and to prevent those who left from returning, about 7,000 have gone home. Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza.

However, no widespread return of those who fled Gaza may be likely until the territory’s prospects are clearer.

“If Gaza returns. If there is an international agreement (with) a comprehensive situation for the Palestinian people and construction begins, why would I delay?” he said.

(Reporting by Nidal al-Mughrabi; Editing by Angus McDowall and Timothy Heritage)
